Spec explainer · NIMBUS-101

Offline Draft Sync

Sample content. Every region of this template holds a worked example for the invented feature NIMBUS-101 Offline Draft Sync, and each one is replaced when the template is filled with a real feature.

TL;DR: NIMBUS-101 keeps the draft editor usable when the connection drops. Edits go into a local queue instead of the network, replay in the order they were made once the connection returns, and any edit that clashes with the stored copy is shown to the author side by side rather than resolved for them. Nothing is discarded without the author seeing it first.

Goals

  • Keep writing through an outage. Opening, editing, and creating a draft all work with no connection, and the editor never blocks on the network.
  • Replay in order. Queued edits are sent in the order the author made them, so a later edit never lands before the one it was built on.
  • Show every clash. Where a queued edit and the stored copy disagree, the author sees both versions and chooses; the feature never picks for them.
  • Say where things stand, in words. Sync state is readable at any moment as queued, replaying, settled, or needs attention.

Non-goals

  • Not offline review. Comments and approvals still need a connection. NIMBUS-101 covers the drafting surface only.
  • Not shared editing while offline. Two authors cannot work on one draft with either of them disconnected.
  • Not background sync. Nothing is sent from a closed tab. The queue replays when the author returns to the draft.
  • Not a change to storage. Once an edit has synced it is stored exactly as it is today, so nothing downstream of the editor has to change.

Acceptance criteria

Editing survives losing the connection mid-sentence

With the connection dropped while the author is typing, the editor keeps accepting input, the caret does not move, and no dialog interrupts. The next keystroke lands in the local queue instead of the network.

Queued edits replay in the order they were made

After four edits made offline and a reconnection, the stored draft matches the editor exactly. Replaying the queue out of order, or in parallel, fails this criterion even when the final text happens to match.

A clash is shown, never resolved quietly

Where the stored copy changed while the author was offline, the two versions are presented together and the author picks one. No clash is merged, dropped, or overwritten without that choice being made.

Sync state is readable without colour

Each of the four states names itself in text. A reader who cannot perceive the hue, and a monochrome screenshot, both still say which state the draft is in.

Clarification FAQ

What happens if the author closes the tab before reconnecting?
The queue stays on that device and replays the next time the same draft is opened there. Nothing is sent from a closed tab, which is what keeps the background-sync non-goal above honest.
How is the order of two devices' queues decided?
It is not. Each device replays its own queue in its own order, and the second device to reconnect is told its edits clash rather than having them interleaved.
Does one clash hold up the rest of the queue?
No. Edits that do not clash settle first, and only the clashing ones wait for the author's choice, so a single disputed paragraph does not strand an hour of offline work.
How long does a queue live before it is discarded?
It is not discarded on a timer. A queue survives until its edits settle or the author abandons them explicitly, because a silent expiry is the one outcome the "nothing is discarded unseen" goal rules out.
